title: Warehouse inventory
intro: A sample to practise the format: a warehouse inventory, built up over four levels. Each level adds to the same class, so later levels reuse your earlier code without breaking it.

levels.spec:
Implement a simplified warehouse inventory. Every method receives a timestamp (an int); timestamps are unique and strictly increasing across calls. A product is identified by its SKU, a string. Quantities are non-negative ints.

add_product(timestamp: int, sku: str, quantity: int) -> bool
Adds a new product with `quantity` units on hand. Returns True if added, False if the SKU already exists (its quantity is left unchanged).

restock(timestamp: int, sku: str, quantity: int) -> int | None
Adds `quantity` units. Returns the new on-hand quantity, or None if the product doesn't exist.

ship(timestamp: int, sku: str, quantity: int) -> int | None
Ships `quantity` units, taking them off hand. Returns the remaining on-hand quantity. Returns None (and changes nothing) if the product doesn't exist or doesn't have `quantity` units.

remove_product(timestamp: int, sku: str) -> bool
Removes the product. True if removed, False if it doesn't exist. A removed SKU can be added again later as a new product.

Examples:
  add_product(1, "APPLE", 10)  -> True
  add_product(2, "APPLE", 5)   -> False   (already exists)
  restock(3, "APPLE", 5)       -> 15
  ship(4, "APPLE", 20)         -> None    (only 15 on hand)
  ship(5, "APPLE", 15)         -> 0
  restock(6, "PEAR", 1)        -> None    (no such product)
  remove_product(7, "APPLE")   -> True
  remove_product(8, "APPLE")   -> False

Reports on what moves and what is running low.

top_shipped(timestamp: int, n: int) -> list[str]
The top n existing products by total units shipped since they were added, as "<sku>(<total>)". Sort by total, descending; break ties by SKU, ascending (plain string order). Products that shipped nothing count with 0. Fewer than n products: return all. Removed products are left out. Failed shipments don't count.

low_stock(timestamp: int, threshold: int) -> list[str]
Every existing product whose on-hand quantity is strictly below `threshold`, as "<sku>(<quantity>)". Sort by quantity, ascending; break ties by SKU, ascending.

Examples (A, B and C each added with 10):
  ship(4, "A", 2)      -> 8
  ship(5, "B", 5)      -> 5
  ship(6, "C", 2)      -> 8
  top_shipped(7, 2)    -> ["B(5)", "A(2)"]
  top_shipped(8, 5)    -> ["B(5)", "A(2)", "C(2)"]
  low_stock(9, 8)      -> ["B(5)"]
  low_stock(10, 9)     -> ["B(5)", "A(8)", "C(8)"]

hidden.name: re added product starts from zero

levels.spec:
Customers can reserve units for a limited time before buying them.

A reservation holds units of a product. Held units stay on hand but are not available: they can't be shipped or reserved by anyone else. Available = on hand minus the units held by the product's active reservations. A reservation made at `timestamp` with `ttl` expires at timestamp + ttl: from then on (any call with a timestamp greater than or equal to it) it is inactive and its units are available again. Expiry never changes on-hand.

Changes: ship now needs `quantity` AVAILABLE units. remove_product also cancels the product's active reservations. low_stock keeps using on-hand, not available.

reserve(timestamp: int, sku: str, quantity: int, ttl: int) -> str | None
Holds `quantity` units for `ttl`. Returns the reservation ID: "res1" for the first successful reservation in the whole system, "res2" for the second, and so on. None (and nothing changes, the ID counter included) if the product doesn't exist or has fewer than `quantity` available units.

confirm(timestamp: int, reservation_id: str) -> bool
The customer buys the held units: they are shipped (off hand, counted in top_shipped) and the reservation ends. True on success; False if it doesn't exist, expired, was already confirmed, or was cancelled.

get_available(timestamp: int, sku: str) -> int | None
The available quantity, or None if the product doesn't exist.

Examples:
  add_product(1, "A", 10)     -> True
  reserve(2, "A", 4, 10)      -> "res1"   (expires at 12)
  get_available(3, "A")       -> 6
  ship(4, "A", 7)             -> None     (only 6 available)
  ship(5, "A", 6)             -> 4        (on hand 4, all held by res1)
  get_available(11, "A")      -> 0
  get_available(12, "A")      -> 4        (res1 expired at 12)
  confirm(13, "res1")         -> False
  reserve(14, "A", 3, 5)      -> "res2"
  confirm(15, "res2")         -> True
  top_shipped(16, 1)          -> ["A(9)"]

hidden.name: expiry does not touch on hand

levels.spec:
Duplicate products get merged, and the warehouse wants to look back in time.

merge_products(timestamp: int, target_sku: str, source_sku: str) -> bool
Merges the source product into the target. False (and nothing changes) if the SKUs are the same or either product doesn't exist. Otherwise: the source's on-hand is added to the target's; the source's total shipped is added to the target's; the source's active reservations now belong to the target (confirming one ships from the target); the source no longer exists (its SKU can be added again as a new product). Returns True.

get_on_hand_at(timestamp: int, sku: str, time_at: int) -> int | None
The on-hand quantity the product had right after the call at `time_at` (or, if nothing happened then, after the last call before it). None if no product with this SKU existed at that time. time_at <= timestamp. If a SKU was removed (or merged away) and added again, each period is answered from the product that existed then.

Examples:
  add_product(1, "A", 5)          -> True
  add_product(2, "B", 3)          -> True
  ship(3, "B", 1)                 -> 2
  restock(4, "A", 5)              -> 10
  merge_products(5, "A", "B")     -> True    (A: on hand 12, shipped 1)
  get_available(6, "B")           -> None
  top_shipped(7, 5)               -> ["A(1)"]
  get_on_hand_at(8, "A", 1)       -> 5
  get_on_hand_at(9, "A", 3)       -> 5
  get_on_hand_at(10, "A", 5)      -> 12
  get_on_hand_at(11, "B", 4)      -> 2
  get_on_hand_at(12, "B", 5)      -> None
  get_on_hand_at(13, "A", 0)      -> None

hidden.name: history across remove and re add

complexity: O(1) per add, restock and ship apart from summing a product's holds (O(r) over active reservations); O(n log n) per ranking; O(log h) per look-back with bisect over a product's history
